author: linyueqian
body:
P2: This re-keys the cross-attn modulation sources for the released LTX-2 and LTX-2.3 paths, not just 2.5. On main, `av_cross_attn_video_scale_shift` took the video timestep and the a2v gate took the audio sigma. Neither branch of `use_cross_timestep` reproduces that combination: with the flag on (2.3 and 2.5) the video scale_shift input switches from the masked per-token video timestep to the uniform audio sigma; with it off (LTX-2) the a2v gate switches from the audio sigma to the masked video timestep. T2V is unaffected since all four sources are numerically equal there, but under I2V the video timestep is zeroed on conditioning-frame tokens, so LTX-2 and LTX-2.3 I2V outputs change. These embeddings are consumed whenever AV cross attention runs (line 1115), independent of the adaln flags.

Can you confirm both re-keyings match the pinned official implementations for 2 and 2.3, and share a run of the `ltx2_3_i2v` accuracy case on this head? Note there is no LTX-2 I2V accuracy case, so that side currently has no guard.

author: linyueqian
body:
P2: `preserves_reference_image_size` is keyed on the `LTX2Pipeline` class, which also serves LTX-2 and LTX-2.3. For those versions the server previously LANCZOS-resized the reference image to the requested WxH, which made the pipeline's aspect-preserving resize plus center crop a no-op. With the server resize skipped, off-aspect inputs are now center-cropped instead of squashed, so legacy online I2V framing changes. The offline example still applies the LANCZOS squash for non-2.5 inputs (`prepare_primary_image`), so offline and online now disagree for 2/2.3.

If restoring the official preprocessing for legacy online I2V is intended, this deserves a release-note line; otherwise the flag needs to be version-conditional rather than class-wide.

author: linyueqian
body: P2: The flip itself looks correct. The guidance executor fuses every pass into the batch dimension and calls the transformer once per denoise step, so `has_separate_cfg=True` (from #2527) made Cache-DiT advance its step counter at the wrong rate for LTX. But Cache-DiT is documented as supported for LTX-2/2.3, so thresholds tuned under the old counting are stale after this change. A quick re-validation of the legacy Cache-DiT path, or at least a release-note callout, would cover it.

author: linyueqian
body: Nit: `_run_diffusers` requires `request["sigmas"]`, but `_run_omni` forwards only the `video_*`/`audio_*` keys, so the Omni side silently ignores this key and falls back to the recipe schedule. Parity holds today because `LTX_DISTILLED_SIGMAS` equals these 8 values plus the terminal 0. If either side drifts, the test would compare different schedules without failing loudly. Consider forwarding `sigmas` through the extra args on the omni backend too, or asserting the recipe schedule matches the request.

author: hsliuustc0106
body:
[P1] Official LTX-2.5 parity fails at the pinned revisions

I ran this exact added test at head `e2721dc97d48a412128327039b2a80bb07c5b0ea` on one NVIDIA L20X (Python 3.12.13, vLLM 0.27.0, vLLM-Omni `0.27.0rc2.dev60+ge2721dc97`, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu129):

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 HF_HOME=/workspace/model \
python -m pytest -q -s \
  'tests/e2e/accuracy/ltx/test_ltx25_official_similarity.py::test_ltx25_distilled_two_stage_matches_official[t2v]'
```

The harness resolved official source `7954dcb0d986bdc36ef272564a9789ade07fcc65`, raw model `8a4ff96f581e72bedc1b44367581c49d544a05f1`, and Diffusers model `a6de4b5354f078db24d9cf4778c14846788aea3d`; both sides used `torch_sdpa`, seed 42, 1024x576, 25 frames, and the same 8+3 schedules. It nevertheless failed in 322.35 s with video SSIM mean/min `0.66285/0.65434` (required `0.995/0.99`), PSNR `17.812 dB` (required `40`), LPIPS `0.36954` (required `<=0.01`), audio cosine `0.14073` (required `>=0.95`), and relative L2 `2.59623` (required `<=0.3`). Because the two runtimes run sequentially on the same device/backend and the mismatch is this large, this does not look like a minor L20X-vs-H100 tolerance difference. Please reproduce and fix the official/Omni trajectory mismatch before treating this parity coverage as passing.

For comparison, the public pipelines themselves are runnable locally. These recipe commands both exited 0 and produced valid H.264 + 48 kHz stereo AAC MP4s:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 HF_HOME=/workspace/model python \
  examples/offline_inference/text_to_video/text_to_video.py \
  --model Lightricks/LTX-2.5-Diffusers \
  --model-class-name LTX2DistilledOneStagePipeline \
  --prompt 'A cinematic shot of a red fox walking through a snowy forest at dawn, the camera tracking alongside, snow crunching underfoot.' \
  --height 544 --width 960 --num-frames 121 --num-inference-steps 8 \
  --frame-rate 24 --fps 24 --enforce-eager --output ltx25-distilled-one-stage.mp4

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 HF_HOME=/workspace/model python \
  examples/offline_inference/text_to_video/text_to_video.py \
  --model Lightricks/LTX-2.5-Diffusers \
  --model-class-name LTX2DistilledTwoStagePipeline \
  --prompt 'A cinematic shot of a red fox walking through a snowy forest at dawn, the camera tracking alongside, snow crunching underfoot.' \
  --height 1088 --width 1920 --num-frames 121 --num-inference-steps 8 \
  --frame-rate 24 --fps 24 --enforce-eager --output ltx25-distilled-two-stage.mp4
```

Observed one-stage: 9.42 s generation, 78,666 MiB peak, 960x544/121 frames/5.042 s. Observed two-stage: 23.58 s generation, 111,716 MiB peak, 1920x1088/121 frames/5.042 s. The focused CPU-safe pipeline file also passed: `36 passed in 2.70s`.

author: lishunyang12
body:
Resolved at current head `8ce11ef77`.

The `e2721dc97` harness selected generic PyTorch SDPA independently in the two runtimes; the `torch_sdpa` metadata did not pin the same kernel. Kernel selection differed by shape/runtime on L20X, which explains the trajectory-scale mismatch. The permanent guard now selects BF16 cuDNN explicitly on both sides: native uses `PytorchAttention(priority=[CUDNN_ATTENTION, MATH])`, while Omni uses `CUDNN_ATTN`; MATH remains only the one-token fallback.

A second issue affected Full two-stage I2V: multiplying Python `noise_scale=0.909375` by a BF16 conditioning mask rounded it early to `0.91015625`. The mask arithmetic now stays FP32. After the fix, native and Omni are bitwise exact at Stage 1 output, Stage 2 input, and Stage 2 final packed latent.

Current B300/cu130 BF16-cuDNN decoded parity for all six public native T2V/I2V paths is:

| Path | Task | SSIM mean/min | PSNR | LPIPS |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Full one-stage | T2V | 0.999652 / 0.999564 | 58.80 dB | 0.0000367 |
| Full one-stage | I2V | 0.999589 / 0.999480 | 62.37 dB | 0.0000576 |
| Full two-stage | T2V | 0.999588 / 0.999485 | 56.40 dB | 0.0000687 |
| Full two-stage | I2V | 0.999585 / 0.999475 | 62.10 dB | 0.0000627 |
| Distilled two-stage | T2V | 0.997186 / 0.996164 | 46.04 dB | 0.003450 |
| Distilled two-stage | I2V | 0.996489 / 0.995810 | 46.29 dB | 0.003787 |

The thresholds now require SSIM mean/min >= 0.99 and PSNR >= 40 dB on every public path. The focused affected CPU suite is `111 passed`. Please rerun the pinned test on current head; it now exercises an explicit cross-runtime cuDNN contract instead of architecture-dependent generic SDPA dispatch.

author: mglyn
body: Could we derive the expected checkpoint kind from `pipeline_kind` instead of storing it in every component profile? The base LTX-2/LTX-2.3 one-stage profiles currently leave this as `None`, so `validate_ltx_checkpoint()` returns early and `LTX2Pipeline` can accept a merged-distilled checkpoint while executing the regular CFG/STG recipe. A single mapping (`one_stage`/`two_stage` -> regular, distilled entries -> distilled, DMD2 -> unchecked) removes duplicate state and closes that gap.

body: Could we pin the process-wide SDPA state here in the same way as the existing LTX-2.3 accuracy guard (`torch.backends.cuda.enable_cudnn_sdp(False)` before model construction)? This module-op override covers the connector and DiT paths, but not Gemma/the text encoder. Since importing vLLM changes the global CUDA SDP state while the standalone official process may retain a different state, H100/H200 may route Gemma attention through different implementations, creating a reproducibility risk for these strict parity thresholds. Would mirroring the LTX-2.3 global pin so both runners use the same process-wide state make the test conditions more reproducible?

author: mglyn
body:
Could we make a reduced CI resolution together with layerwise offload the preferred configuration for these two-stage cases, similar to the existing LTX-2.3 accuracy guard? Both variants load the x2 upsampler, and the Full path additionally materializes the large refinement LoRA, so their representative 1080p configurations exceed a single 80 GB H100.
The current tests appear to already use reduced shapes and pass --enable-layerwise-offload; could we verify and record the actual peak memory under this exact CI configuration to ensure sufficient H100 headroom?
If that is still insufficient, moving the cases to a higher-memory runner or removing them from this job would be preferable. TP or VAE tiling could be fallback options, but both materially change numerical behavior, so they would likely require rebaselined and relaxed accuracy thresholds.

author: hsliuustc0106
body: The blanket `except Exception` here silently degrades version detection to `"2"` on a transient hub error (network blip, partial cache). That is not just cosmetic: detection feeds `should_preserve_reference_image_size` and the DiT config subfolder (`transformer_full` vs `transformer`), so a one-off download failure at startup can flip the resize semantics and load the wrong transformer config for the lifetime of the process — and `serving_video.py` caches the detection in a `cached_property`, so it never recovers. Could we at least `logger.debug/warn` the swallowed exception so this is diagnosable in the wild? Narrowing to `(OSError, requests exceptions, EntryNotFoundError)` would also keep genuinely-missing metadata on the fast path.
